head: Model (balanced acc., %)
Collagen Pepsin
Lichens 1
Lichens 2
notes: Format: 19 Oct sweep (shifted labels) -> rerun with recorded wavelengths (difference; matched repeat/fold units). Spectral models 15/4/10 units, spatial attention 6/4/4.

Outcome: no attention model has the highest mean on any dataset any more. Best proposed vs best baseline: Pepsin ex_tokens 90.0 vs LR 90.3 (-0.3 [-4.7, +3.0]); Lichens 1 SmartAttn v0 99.2 vs SpectralFormer 99.5 (-0.2); Lichens 2 ex_tokens 86.1 vs RBF-SVM 86.6 (-0.5). No corrected-test p < 0.05 anywhere. The paper's conclusion (competitive, not superior) is unchanged; the 'highest overall mean on Pepsin' claim is removed.
Spatial: spatial attention 91.0 vs patch-mean RF 86.4 on Pepsin (+4.5 [-0.8, +9.6], n.s.); below the 2D-CNN on both lichen sets.

Importance: the earlier above-chance overlap between attention rankings and the Autoencoder-paper selection (Pepsin 13 of 30, p = 0.0005) did not replicate after retraining (2 of 30, p = 0.99; Lichens 1 1 of 13, last-layer 3 of 13, p = 0.047). This claim is withdrawn from the paper.
The changes (-2.2 to +3.1 points) are within the fold-to-fold spread; GPU run-to-run variation was not measured separately.
